name: Premiere Text Pop Scale Preset
use_when: Center text or emphasis text needs a quick energetic entrance in Premiere.
A text phrase is more important than ordinary captions but does not need a full AE animation.
The editor wants a reusable Transform preset for repeated brand text.
avoid_when: The text is a normal subtitle and pop motion would become irritating.
The project tone is serious and a bounce/pop would feel cheap.
The text would cover a face, proof, product, or key action.

timeline_pattern.pattern: text_layer -> brand_style -> transform_scale_70 -> 7_frames_scale_110 -> 5_frames_scale_100 -> optional_ease -> glow_or_glitch_if_style_fit -> save_preset
timeline_pattern.text_job_rule: Use this for center/emphasis text or scene text, not every caption.
timeline_pattern.preset_rule: Save the Transform animation as a named preset only after testing it on multiple text lengths.
timeline_pattern.brand_rule: Font, color, glow, and glitch settings should match the channel style.

motion.rule: Use a short overshoot pop that arrives quickly and settles before the viewer needs to read the phrase.

keyframe_values.easing: Smooth keyframes if it improves feel, but keep readability more important than bounce style.

sound.rule: Use a small pop, click, or hit only when the text is a real emphasis beat; keep it below dialogue.

captions.rule: Do not duplicate the same words as captions unless the text needs both accessibility and emphasis.

color.rule: Glow, glitch, and accent colors should improve emphasis without harming readability.

implementation.ffmpeg: Approximate with drawtext alpha and fontsize envelopes, such as a 70% start, optional 110% peak, and 100% settle, while keeping x/y centered from text dimensions.
implementation.remotion: Create a Sequence-local TextPop component with start, overshoot, settle, spring/interpolate settings, safeRegion, and optional glow/glitch style.
implementation.blender: Use text-object scale keyframes with overshoot interpolation for spatial text.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use keyframes or a pop animation preset, then verify the phrase remains readable at phone size.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Apply Transform to the text layer, keyframe Scale at 70%, 110% after about 7 frames, and 100% after about 5 more frames; save as a preset after QC.

common_mistakes: Using pop text on every sentence until it becomes irritating.
Saving the preset before testing long and short phrases.
Letting the bounce finish after the spoken emphasis has passed.
Adding glow or glitch that makes the word harder to read.
qc: Does the text pop finish before or as the phrase is spoken?
Is the phrase readable at delivery size?
Does it avoid faces, proof, products, and captions?
Is the SFX, if used, below dialogue?
Is the preset named by behavior and tested on different text lengths?
